gaps.concept: Beta-cell glucokinase has a high Km and acts as the glucose sensor that sets the threshold for insulin release.
gaps.why_tested: An enzyme-defect stem asks how beta cells detect rising glucose. [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1665/)

gaps.concept: Heterozygous loss-of-function GCK mutations raise the insulin-secretion threshold, causing mild, stable familial hyperglycemia (MODY 2).
gaps.why_tested: A young patient with lifelong mild hyperglycemia and an affected parent points to glucokinase. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK500456/)

gaps.concept: Loss-of-function ABCC8 or KCNJ11 K-ATP channels cause congenital hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; activating variants impair insulin release and cause neonatal diabetes.
gaps.why_tested: A neonatal glucose disorder asks whether the beta-cell potassium channel remains open or closed. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1447/)

gaps.concept: Amino acids stimulate insulin as well as glucagon; the glucagon response prevents hypoglycemia after a protein-rich meal.
gaps.why_tested: A protein-only meal raises insulin without the expected fall in blood glucose. [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3538843/)

gaps.concept: Parasympathetic M3 and sympathetic β2 signaling stimulate insulin secretion; sympathetic α2 signaling inhibits it.
gaps.why_tested: An adrenergic or vagal stimulus asks for the direction of beta-cell secretion. [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1689116/)

gaps.concept: Delta-cell somatostatin locally inhibits both insulin and glucagon secretion.
gaps.why_tested: An islet paracrine-signaling stem asks what delta cells do to neighboring cells. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279127/)

gaps.concept: GIP comes from intestinal K cells; GLP-1 comes from L cells, suppresses glucagon, and slows gastric emptying.
gaps.why_tested: An oral-glucose or incretin-drug stem asks which gut cell or effect is involved. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279141/table/pharmaco-agent-diab2.T.characteristics_o/)

gaps.concept: DPP-4 degrades GLP-1 and GIP; DPP-4 inhibitors prolong their glucose-dependent insulinotropic effect.
gaps.why_tested: A drug-mechanism stem asks why inhibiting an incretin-degrading enzyme increases meal-stimulated insulin. [Endotext](https://www.endotext.org/wp-content/uploads/pdfs/oral-and-injectable-non-insulin-pharmacological-agents-for-type-2-diabetes.pdf)

gaps.concept: Beta cells co-secrete amylin with insulin; amylin suppresses meal-related glucagon release and slows gastric emptying.
gaps.why_tested: A missing beta-cell peptide or amylin-analog stem asks for its postprandial effects. [NCBI](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/1642707/)

gaps.concept: Pancreatic alpha cells cleave proglucagon with PC2 to make glucagon; intestinal L cells use PC1/3 to make GLP-1.
gaps.why_tested: A peptide-processing stem asks why one precursor yields different hormones in pancreas and gut. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279127/)

gaps.concept: The glucagon receptor is Gs-coupled and activates adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and protein kinase A, chiefly in hepatocytes.
gaps.why_tested: A receptor-signaling stem asks which second messenger drives hepatic glucose output. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279127/)

gaps.concept: Glucagon does not directly mobilize skeletal-muscle glycogen; muscle glycogen supports local ATP production and cannot supply free blood glucose.
gaps.why_tested: A fasting or exercise stem contrasts liver glucose output with muscle glycogen use. [NCBI](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3005043/)

gaps.concept: Hepatocyte glucose transport uses insulin-independent GLUT2, although insulin regulates hepatic glucose storage and production.
gaps.why_tested: A tissue-comparison stem asks why liver glucose entry differs from muscle and adipose uptake. [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1671/box/A31/)

gaps.concept: Insulin promotes glycogen storage through phosphatase-mediated glycogen-synthase activation; glucagon-driven phosphorylation activates glycogen phosphorylase and inhibits glycogen synthase.
gaps.why_tested: An enzyme-activity stem asks which glycogen enzyme is active after feeding versus fasting. [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28731034/)

gaps.concept: In liver, glucagon lowers fructose-2,6-bisphosphate via PFK-2/FBPase-2 phosphorylation, suppressing glycolysis and favoring gluconeogenesis; insulin reverses this.
gaps.why_tested: An enzyme-regulation stem asks how the two hormones switch hepatic glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. [NCBI](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7778149/)

gaps.concept: Insulin stimulates adipose lipoprotein lipase for circulating triglyceride uptake and inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase that mobilizes stored fat.
gaps.why_tested: A lipid-enzyme stem distinguishes triglyceride delivery to adipose tissue from release of stored fatty acids. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK305896/)

gaps.concept: Insulin activates acetyl-CoA carboxylase; its product malonyl-CoA inhibits CPT1, limiting fatty-acid oxidation and ketogenesis.
gaps.why_tested: A fed-versus-fasted enzyme stem asks why fatty-acid synthesis and oxidation move in opposite directions. [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK493179/)

gaps.concept: Muscle contraction recruits GLUT4 independently of insulin, increasing glucose uptake during exercise.
gaps.why_tested: An exercise stem asks why working muscle takes up glucose despite low circulating insulin. [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7836174/)

gaps.concept: Fasting glucose production shifts from hepatic glycogenolysis toward gluconeogenesis using lactate, glycerol, and glucogenic amino acids as glycogen is depleted.
gaps.why_tested: A prolonged-fast stem asks for the principal glucose source or its precursor. [NCBI](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5293555/)

gaps.concept: During prolonged fasting, hepatic fatty-acid oxidation supplies acetyl-CoA for ketogenesis as oxaloacetate is diverted to gluconeogenesis.
gaps.why_tested: A starvation stem asks why excess acetyl-CoA becomes ketone bodies. [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK493179/)

gaps.concept: The liver makes but cannot consume ketone bodies because it lacks thiophorase; erythrocytes cannot use ketones because they lack mitochondria.
gaps.why_tested: A fuel-use stem asks which tissues can oxidize ketones during starvation. [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK493179/)

gaps.concept: Falling insulin is the first defense against hypoglycemia; glucagon and epinephrine act rapidly, whereas cortisol and growth hormone act later.
gaps.why_tested: A hypoglycemia time-course stem asks which hormonal response occurs first. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279137/)

gaps.concept: Sulfonylurea-induced hypoglycemia raises both insulin and C-peptide like insulinoma; a positive sulfonylurea screen distinguishes them.
gaps.why_tested: A fasting-hypoglycemia stem has high endogenous insulin markers and asks for the discriminating test. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278981/)

gaps.concept: Inappropriately high insulin during hypoglycemia suppresses lipolysis and ketogenesis, producing low free fatty acids and β-hydroxybutyrate.
gaps.why_tested: A hypoglycemia laboratory panel asks whether the episode is insulin mediated. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279137/table/hypoglycemia.T.distinguishing_causes_of/)

gaps.concept: Diazoxide opens beta-cell K-ATP channels, hyperpolarizing the membrane and reducing insulin secretion.
gaps.why_tested: A drug-mechanism stem asks for the functional opposite of sulfonylurea action. [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9519741/)
